findings.evidence: plugins/specflow/skills/complete/SKILL.md:273-279 — Phase E.4 schema validation enumerates two checks: (1) every top-level key matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`; (2) every top-level key is in the allow-list (the 25 fields named in the Schema Appendix). Cross-checking against the PRD Schema Appendix (lines 141-176 of `003-complete-skill-prd.md`) — the appendix names exactly 25 top-level fields (`id`, `feature`, `task_id`, `title`, `scope`, `completed_at`, `triggered_by`, `lane_assigned`, `ai_assistance_level`, `elapsed_minutes`, `what_worked`, `what_didnt_work`, `blast_radius_outcome`, `superseded_by_retro`, `actual_hours`, `regressions_caught`, `escaped_issues`, `accepted_with_failure`, `elevation_offered`, `elevation_fired_by`, `elevation_outcome`, `decision_log_links`, `scope_change_log`, `addenda`, `prd_anchor`). The SKILL body's E.4 says 'extraneous keys are a failed write' but does NOT say 'missing required keys are a failed write'. So an entry that drops a required field (e.g. omits `prd_anchor` entirely on a fresh-entry write) would pass E.4's two documented checks (no extraneous key; remaining keys snake_case) and still be malformed. The E.6 verify step says 'The entry validates against the schema (E.4 passed)' but if E.4 doesn't check required-field presence, neither does E.6.
findings.claim: Schema validation under-checks — E.4 rejects extraneous fields and validates field-name format but does not validate required-field presence. The PRD AC-3 mandates non-null values for `actual_hours`, `regressions_caught`, `escaped_issues`; AC-5 mandates the field set in the Schema Appendix is the allow-list (forward + reverse). E.4 enforces only one direction (no fields outside the list). A malformed entry missing a required field would slip through. This is a correctness defect, not a calibration concern — the SKILL body would write malformed entries that the schema-stability surface (E.4) was designed to prevent.
findings.proposed_change: Add a third check at E.4: 'Every required field from the Schema Appendix is present in the entry (count: 25 for fresh-entry; supersede-path checks the seven mutable fields and the unchanged required fields). Missing required fields are a failed write — refuse with: "Schema violation: missing required field `{name}`. Refusing write." Release lock; exit.' The required-field list should be enumerated explicitly (the same 25-field list at the allow-list in check 2). This closes the asymmetric-validation gap.

findings.evidence: plugins/specflow/skills/complete/SKILL.md:62 — Phase A.3 specifies the lock path as `admin/scratch/complete-{task-id}.lock`. Cross-checking against `skills/develop/SKILL.md` Phase F.6 (lines 569-571 of develop SKILL.md): 'rm -rf admin/scratch/{NNN-slug}-develop/'. The develop scratch directory pattern is `admin/scratch/{NNN-slug}-develop/` (per-feature). The complete skill's lock path is `admin/scratch/complete-{task-id}.lock` (per-task, sibling-to-feature-scratch-dir). There is no immediate collision because the lock filename has `complete-` prefix, but if `specflow:develop` Phase F.6 runs `rm -rf admin/scratch/{NNN-slug}-develop/` while `specflow:complete` is mid-flight (auto-fire scenario where develop's F.6 fires before complete's H.1 releases the lock — this is the exact F.5 → F.6 boundary the SKILL header at line 21 names), the lock file at `admin/scratch/complete-{task-id}.lock` is OUTSIDE the `{NNN-slug}-develop/` directory and would be preserved. Good. BUT the lane-assignments scratch directory at `admin/scratch/003-complete-skill-develop/` IS inside the `{NNN-slug}-develop/` pattern — so when this very skill (003-complete-skill) runs through `specflow:develop` and reaches Phase F.6 cleanup, it would `rm -rf` its own develop scratch directory. The lock file at the sibling path survives. The SKILL body should explicitly note that the lock path is outside the develop-scratch convention to make the orthogonality observable.
findings.claim: Path-orthogonality assumption is correct but undocumented — the lock at `admin/scratch/complete-{task-id}.lock` is intentionally outside the `{NNN-slug}-develop/` cleanup scope so develop's Phase F.6 cleanup does not race with complete's Phase H.1 lock release. The SKILL body does not document this orthogonality. A reader unfamiliar with `specflow:develop`'s F.6 would not know whether the lock path is collision-safe.
findings.proposed_change: Add a one-line note at Phase A.3 (after the lock-path declaration): 'Lock path is intentionally outside `admin/scratch/{NNN-slug}-develop/` to remain unaffected by `specflow:develop` Phase F.6 cleanup; the lock survives across the F.5 → F.6 boundary that auto-fires this skill.' This documents the orthogonality so future skill authors do not move the lock path inside the develop-scratch directory pattern.
